_comment: Hand-authored place-type templates for /simulate's routine/arc mechanism (design debrief 2026-08-10, renamed from archetypes.json to contexts.json 2026-08-16 - 'archetype' read as describing the character, when it's actually the shared context a routine happens in). A context is authored once here, not per character - texture and 'provides' are shared by every routine tagged with this context. A character's routine references one of these by name plus a one-line personal routine_actions entry (see character SKILL.md). Starter set below covers the place-types already implied by the existing cast (Terfila as a port/market town, Görff as workshop/archive territory, the Feria as a waystation of sorts) - expand by hand as new routines need a place-type that isn't here yet, same discipline as everything else authored rather than generated in this system. `grounding_provides` (added 2026-08-26) is a separate field from `provides`: it gates which _lore/grounding/mechanics.json entries a character with this routine context knows (scripts/lore/sample_grounding.py), a different concern from `provides`, which drives arc-need matching via check_needs_provides.py. An empty grounding_provides list is a real, intentional choice for a context with no physical-mechanics content of its own (an archive keeper doesn't need to know crop-growing conditions), not an oversight - expand per-context as mechanics.json grows. Three new tags added 2026-08-26/27 alongside the exhaustive vanilla-1.20.1 mechanics.json pass, each mapped to the one existing context it fit best rather than inventing a new context: `redstone` -> workshop (an extension of hands-on making, not a separate trade), `alchemy` -> temple (brewing/potions read as a temple's remedies/rites, the closest existing fit to anything resembling medicine), `navigation` -> waystation (portals/maps/biomes are exactly a traveler's-eye-view of the world). Mob/survival-danger content stayed `universal` rather than inventing a `combat` tag/context - same epistemic bar as the original creepers/hunger entries (something anyone alive in this world would know, not specialized trade knowledge) - so no context maps to it.

market.texture: Buying and selling, price disputes, scarcity, trust in a trading partner or supplier, goods that come and go with the season or the ships.

workshop.texture: Making things by hand, materials ordered or scavenged, apprentices, pride or shame in the work's quality, tools that need tending as much as the product does.

archive.texture: Records, attribution, gaps in the record, the physical work of maintaining what's stored, contradictions between sources.

waystation.texture: Travelers passing through, news carried in and out, brief contact that isn't expected to repeat, schedules and delays.

port.texture: Ships arriving and departing, cargo manifests, customs, tides and sailing schedules, news and goods carried in fresh with every crew.

temple.texture: Rites, quiet devotion, disputes over doctrine or upkeep, the material cost of keeping a sacred place running, pilgrims and mourners passing through.

gardens.texture: Growing things, seasons and blight, water rights, quiet unglamorous labor, a green space the rest of the city treats as either a shared resource or an afterthought to fund.

municipality.texture: Permits, disputes referred upward, budgets, the paperwork that makes a city a city, favors owed and called in.

bank.texture: Ledgers, loans, interest, a city's money moving or not moving, trust extended or withdrawn, disputes over debts.
